title: 1951 AHSME Problem 5
statement: Mr. \(A\) owns a home worth \(\$10{,}000.\) He sells it to Mr. \(B\) at a \(10\%\) profit based on the worth of the house. Mr. \(B\) sells the house back to Mr. \(A\) at a \(10\%\) loss. Then:

solutions.text:
The first sale price is \(10{,}000(1.10)=11{,}000.\) The return sale is \(11{,}000(0.90)=9{,}900.\) Mr. \(A\) receives \(11{,}000\) and pays back \(9{,}900,\) so he gains \(1{,}100.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Compute the two sale prices separately
The first sale is for \(10{,}000(1.10)\), and the return sale is \(10\%\) below that amount
